lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Gerald, it's Kendra. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the overnight fast went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Better than last week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What happened with the overnight fast?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 2 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Black coffee, tea or water are fine during the fast. They don't break it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The research is very clear, you have to eat earlier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What could you try instead?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Everybody gets home late, so dinner is late.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Dinner's late at your house.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My sugar was better the weeks I ate earlier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the overnight fast. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Work has been crazy, I'm doing overtime.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Work took over this week.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I told my family I'm done eating at 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Finishing dinner a little earlier, like by 7, makes the 13 hours a lot easier.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, let's say I finish eating by 7:30 on 4 nights.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 6. Maybe 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If work gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the parties made this week harder, you still got 2 days in, and your plan is to finish eating by 7:30 on 4 nights. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Gerald, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Brief acknowledgment, no reflection of content
Ability and planning strategy, social support
Stated goal: keep up with grandkids
Need and reason: fear of recurrence
Observed benefit: better sugar with earlier eating
Adds meaning not voiced; leans toward pushing agenda
Specific plan: finish eating by 7:30, 4 nights
Summary misstates barrier as parties; participant said work

flags.reason: Directive 'You have to make this a priority' after participant said 'I don't know'; no permission asked.
'The research is very clear, you have to eat earlier' pushes advice and undercuts participant autonomy right after ambivalent 'Maybe.'
Participant noted better sugar when eating earlier; coach did not explore or reflect this motivation.
Summary says 'the parties made this week harder' but participant described work overtime as the barrier.

score.summary: Kendra used good open questions and an effective backup-plan prompt that helped Gerald build a specific goal of finishing dinner by 7:30 on four nights. However, she repeatedly pushed directive advice ('you have to make this a priority', 'the research is very clear') and misstated his barrier in the final summary.
strengths: Line 14 and line 26: open questions drew out Gerald's own ideas for making the fast easier.
Line 56: asking about a backup plan for work conflicts prepared him for barriers.
Line 53-57: plan was concrete and Gerald rated confidence at 6-7, a clear commitment.
coaching_tips: Line 18 and 22: replace directives with a reflection or permission request, e.g., 'Would it help to talk about what priority could look like for you?'
Line 31: when Gerald says his sugar was better eating earlier, reflect it and ask what that means to him.
Line 58: summarize using his own words; he named work overtime, not parties.
Line 38 and 40: pair affirmations with autonomy, and avoid praise that sounds like pressure to follow through.
Line 33: avoid adding meaning Gerald did not voice; reflect his stated goal of keeping up with grandkids instead.
